title: Siena nos. 13 and 16: a letter on the Pope and Bologna, deciphered from its plaintext twin

documents.shelfmark: Archivio di Stato di Siena, Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 13; DECODE R4801 (Concistoro_2308_55); plaintext no. 16, DECODE R4804 (Concistoro_2308_58)
documents.date: 1527-1529 (Lautrec at Modena and Reggio, the Pope's coming to Bologna; unverified)
documents.route: unknown writer -> V. S. Ill.ma (a lord or ambassador)

plaintext.source: No. 16 (DECODE R4804), the clear text of the same letter, in the same fascicle.

transcription.notes: 553 cipher symbols on 10 lines with ten clear stretches. Transcription and initial key by Lasry in CTTS; Claude Fable 5.1 finalised the transcription from the plaintext. Count from the report, not re-measured; George Lasry names accurate transcription as the main obstacle in this fascicle.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution, one or two signs per letter (many of them numerals), four doubled-letter signs (ll, gg, ss, cc) and one null, no word codes.

diacritics.note: Several numeral signs carry superscript circles or strokes; their role is not stated in the report.

system.doubled_letters: Four signs for ll, gg, ss, cc.
system.sibling_key: No filed key matched; the plaintext twin no. 16 gave it.

prior_solution.where: No. 16 (R4804) is the clear text of the letter, filed in the same fascicle; the project noted on 24 Sept that no. 16 is the decipherment of no. 13 but did not rebuild the key.

conditions.human_role: George Lasry transcribed and built the initial key in CTTS; Claude Fable 5.1 finalised key and transcription from no. 16. This project filed his report.

solution.what: Project survey (siena1421): no. 16 identified as the clear text of no. 13; partial alignment (bologna, accordi con). Not taken further; listed as deciphered at the time.
George Lasry transcribed the 553 cipher symbols in CTTS and built an initial key.
Claude Fable 5.1 finalised the key and the transcription from the given plaintext of no. 16.
Whole cipher deciphered; first word (baca?) and 'sabbatte' doubtful.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's decipherment and translation (reading.txt, translation.txt, lasry_report.md) and his key figure key_lasry.jpg with the table key.md; no transcription of no. 13 is in the repository (neither his CTTS transcription nor a project one).

validation.notes: contributed reading: George Lasry's sign-level CTTS transcription and key are not in the repository, so no token alignment can be scored

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt from the plaintext copy no. 16 (R4804), filed in the same fascicle.
outcome.fraction_read_source: George Lasry's report: 'Solved'; only the first word and 'sabbatte' doubtful

gaps.item: first word (baca?) and 'sabbatte'; writer, addressee, date
gaps.detail: Doubtful in the report even with the plaintext twin.

credits.note: Transcription and initial key in CTTS; key finalised with Claude Fable 5.1 from the plaintext no. 16 (report pp. 35-36).
credits.source: Email and report to Daniel Bourdeau, 17 Oct 2026

outcome.notes: Contributed; no. 16 (R4804) is the clear copy.

texts.label: No. 13 (R4801), a letter on the Pope and Bologna, [1527-1529] (George Lasry)
texts.summary: To 'V. S. Ill.ma': the Pope's agreements and the delay of his coming to Bologna have left 'qualche ruggine'; the writer would spend everything to abase the neighbours and, claiming some castle, do as Lautrec did when he took Modena and Reggio, 'perché al peggio non si ha sinon a rendere'. Dated 1527-1530 from the content, unverified; no. 16 (R4804) is its clear copy. Decryption and translation are George Lasry's, verbatim from his report; his CTTS transcription is not in the repository.
